# Find human-made references for AI video: light, framing, type, motion

**A video request becomes query packs over 22 open sources and a board of three human-made candidates per job.**

<p><img src="https://s3.varg.ai/files/194b94d0-58ff-4e8b-91de-4f1959d04013/file_c02ffe003ee2.webp" alt="A board of four cinematic references, a woman reading by a lamp, a warmly lit dinner, a modern house at dusk and a sunlit pool, then each reference in turn." width="480"></p>

Find real, human-made references before anything is made, for AI image, video and music and for video made with code. Turns a request into one query pack per job (light first, then framing, people, location, texture, type, motion, palette, music and a "never" board), searches each source in its own words, opens everything it keeps, proves who made it, measures what code can measure, checks light with an LLM judge, and hands a person three candidates per job. Use when someone says "find references", "reference board", "what should this look like", "lighting reference", "framing reference", "texture reference", "font reference", "motion reference", "casting reference", "music reference", "moodboard references", "make it not look like AI", "avoid slop", "rank these references", or starts a video with no look yet. Not for writing the look from chosen references (video-moodboard, varg-video-prompting), building the cast (character-passport) or downloading one known link (media-download).

```bash
npx skills add vargHQ/skills --skill find-references                # Claude Code, Codex, Cursor, Grok, Gemini CLI, OpenCode…
gh skill install vargHQ/skills find-references --agent github-copilot --scope user
# or all 78 skills as a Claude Code plugin:
claude plugin marketplace add vargHQ/skills
claude plugin install varg@varg
```

## Ask your agent

- "Find lighting and framing references for a rainy night bus-stop scene before I generate anything"
- "Make a reference board for a 30-second coffee ad in a 1970s kitchen: light, palette, texture and music"
- "I'm coding a launch video in HyperFrames; find type and motion references so it doesn't look like a template"
